item.title: Israel election live: polls open in most consequential vote in country’s history
item.description:
A Palestinian man stands next to an election banner featuring Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Oct. 6, 2026. Photo by Zain Jaafar/AFP via Getty Images For weeks, as Israel’s election campaign has intensified, the discussion among many has been about the “blocs” that are being formed among political parties: specifically the Netanyahu and the anti-Netanyahu blocs. In examining the “blocs,” the focus is on numbers, on the conscription of the ultra-Orthodox Jews, and ultimately whether this is a referendum on Benjamin Netanyahu himself. And while there’s much genocidal talk, ignored is what this election means for 50% of the population that lives from the River to the Sea: Palestinians. item.title: Brazil: defeated Flávio Bolsonaro ordered to surrender passports
item.description:
This article was published in partnership with Agência Pública , Brazil’s largest nonprofit newsroom . Two weeks before the second and decisive round of the Brazilian presidential elections in October, US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. was in Rio de Janeiro for the multiday celebration of his son Conor’s wedding . The Kennedy scion married singer Giulia Be, a pop star born into a Brazilian right-wing clan, the Marinho family, who are close allies of the disgraced former President Jair Bolsonaro. The nuptials took place at the Our Lady of Mount Carmel Church in historic downtown Rio, which once served the Portuguese royalty that colonized Brazil for more than 300 years. A week later, supporters of then-presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro carried an inflatable missile with the words “Trump nuke Brazil” in English at a rally in the city of São Paulo. item.title: How ICE Operates in the Shadows
item.description:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents on March 24, 2026 in New York, New York. —Michael M. Santiago—Getty Images During the presidential election of 1863, at the height of the Civil War, federal troops reportedly descended on polling places in Delaware, Kentucky, Maryland, and Missouri and prevented people they deemed disloyal from voting. This prompted a fierce national debate that culminated in Congress passing an 1865 law barring federal “troops or armed men” from “any place” where an election is being held. The central goal of this law, according to its proponents, was “to prevent the President and his officers from interfering in elections,” which are run by the states. Keeping armed federal officers away from the polls, they argued, was necessary to preserve democracy, even in the midst of civil war. This has been the clear law, and the respected policy of every…

item.title: Mbappé dropped by major Chinese brands drop as backlash grows over Mao joke
item.description:
French football star Kylian Mbappé was dropped by two major Chinese brands on Tuesday after a video circulated online in which he appeared to joke about former leader Mao Zedong. Energy drink giant Dongpeng and dairy producer Mengniu said they had terminated their partnerships, citing remarks that offended Chinese national sentiment.

item.title: Brewers rout the Rays 10-1 to move within a win of their first World Series title
item.description:
The Milwaukee Brewers moved one step closer to their first ever World Series title on Monday night, taking a 3-0 series lead with a dominant 10-1 win. That's the short version of the story. The long version? The Tampa Bay Rays will be kicking themselves over a disastrous top of the fifth inning, and historians will one day use a clip of that inning, and the entire 2026 Brewers' postseason run for that matter, as proof of how powerful luck is in Major League Baseball. Game three meant the series shifted to Tampa Bay, and Tropicana Field was packed to the rafters with Rays fans and a sizable contingent of Brewers supporters. But as has typically been the case this postseason , only those in Milwaukee blue and gold had much to cheer about. item.title: Jordan carries out deadly strike in Syria in retaliation for church attack
item.description:
Jordanian air force says it carried out strikes against ‘terrorist groups’ tied to killing of nine during funeral Jordan has carried out airstrikes against armed groups in Syria in retaliation for Friday’s attack on a Greek Orthodox church in the southern Jordanian governorate of Karak that killed nine people, the Jordanian air force has said in a statement. It said the operation “resulted in the killing and wounding of many members of these terrorist groups and the destruction of a number of their vehicles”. It did not specify who the groups were or the precise location of the strikes. Continue reading...

item.title: Ex-South Carolina governors endorse Democrat Annie Andrews in Senate race
item.description:
Republican and Democrat come together for a rare joint endorsement of candidate in unexpected competitive race Two South Carolina former governors, David Beasley and Jim Hodges, a Republican and Democrat respectively, have come together for a rare joint endorsement for Democrat Annie Andrews’s Senate bid. Andrews, a pediatrician, is looking to flip the seat , currently held by Darline Graham, the Trump-endorsed sister of the late senator Lindsey Graham, in what has become an unexpectedly competitive race for the usually reliably red state.
